pairs: Naaman princeps militiæ regis Syriæ erat vir magnus apud dominum suum,
the leader of the military of the king of Syria,
per illum enim dedit Dominus salutem Syriæ:
was a great and honorable man with his lord.
For through him the Lord gave salvation to Syria.
And he was a strong and rich man,
Porro de Syria egressi fuerant latrunculi,
Now robbers had gone out from Syria,
et captivam duxerant de terra Israël puellam parvulam,
and they had led away captive, from the land of Israel, a little girl.
quæ erat in obsequio uxoris Naaman:
And she was in the service of the wife of Naaman.
And she said to her lady:
Utinam fuisset dominus meus ad prophetam qui est in Samaria,
“I wish that my lord had been with the prophet who is in Samaria. Certainly,
profecto curasset eum a lepra quam habet.
he would have cured him of the leprosy that he has.”
Ingressus est itaque Naaman ad dominum suum,
et sic locuta est puella de terra Israël.
“The girl from the land of Israel spoke in such a manner.”
And the king of Syria said to him,
et mittam litteras ad regem Israël.
and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.”
And when he had set out,
et tulisset secum decem talenta argenti,
he had taken with him ten talents of silver,
and ten changes of fine clothing.
detulit litteras ad regem Israël in hæc verba:
And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, in these words:
scito quod miserim ad te Naaman servum meum,
know that I have sent to you my servant, Naaman,
ut cures eum a lepra sua.
so that you may heal him of his leprosy.”
And when the king of Israel had read the letter,
et ait: Numquid deus ego sum,
so that I could take or give life,
quia iste misit ad me ut curem hominem a lepra sua?
or so that this man would send to me to cure a man from his leprosy?
animadvertite, et videte quod occasiones quærat adversum me.
Take notice and see that he is seeking occasions against me.”
Quod cum audisset Eliseus vir Dei,
And when Elisha, the man of God, had heard this,
scidisse videlicet regem Israël vestimenta sua,
specifically, that the king of Israel had torn his garments,
et sciat esse prophetam in Israël.
and let him know that there is a prophet in Israel.”
Naaman arrived with his horses and chariots,
et stetit ad ostium domus Elisei:
and he stood at the door of the house of Elisha.
And Elisha sent a messenger to him,
and wash seven times in the Jordan,
and your flesh will receive health,
And becoming angry, Naaman went away,
“I thought that he would have come out to me, and,
et stans invocaret nomen Domini Dei sui,
standing, would have invoked the name of the Lord, his God,
et tangeret manu sua locum lepræ,
and that he would have touched the place of the leprosy with his hand,
Numquid non meliores sunt Abana et Pharphar fluvii Damasci,
Are not the Abana and the Pharpar,
better than all the waters of Israel,
so that I might wash in them and be cleansed?”
after he had turned himself away and was leaving with indignation,
his servants approached him, and they said to him:
etsi rem grandem dixisset tibi propheta, certe facere debueras:
to do something great, certainly you ought to have done it.
quanto magis quia nunc dixit tibi:
How much more so, now that he has said to you:
Descendit, et lavit in Jordane septies juxta sermonem viri Dei:
So he descended and washed in the Jordan seven times, in accord with the word of the man of God.
et restituta est caro ejus sicut caro pueri parvuli,
And his flesh was restored, like the flesh of a little child.
Reversusque ad virum Dei cum universo comitatu suo,
And returning to the man of God, with his entire retinue, he arrived,
and stood before him, and he said:
Vere scio quod non sit alius deus in universa terra,
I know there is no other God, in all the earth,
Obsecro itaque ut accipias benedictionem a servo tuo.
And so I beg you to accept a blessing from your servant.”
And though he urged him strongly,
he did not agree at all.
But I beg you to grant to me,
concede mihi servo tuo ut tollam onus duorum burdonum de terra:
that I may take from here the burden of two mules from the ground.
non enim faciet ultra servus tuus holocaustum aut victimam diis alienis,
For your servant will no longer offer holocaust or victim to other gods,
But there is still this matter,
de quo depreceris Dominum pro servo tuo, quando ingredietur dominus meus templum Remmon ut adoret:
for which you will entreat the Lord on behalf of your servant: when my lord enters the temple of Rimmon,
et illo innitente super manum meam,
so that he may adore there, and he leans on my hand,
if I will bow down in the temple of Rimmon,
while he is adoring in the same place,
ut ignoscat mihi Dominus servo tuo pro hac re.
that the Lord may ignore me, your servant, concerning this matter.”
Abiit ergo ab eo electo terræ tempore.
Then he went away from him, in the elect time of the earth.
And Gehazi, the servant of the man of God,
Pepercit dominus meus Naaman Syro isti,
said: “My lord has spared Naaman, this Syrian,
ut non acciperet ab eo quæ attulit:
by not receiving from him what he brought.
Et secutus est Giezi post tergum Naaman:
And so, Gehazi followed after the back of Naaman.
quem cum vidisset ille currentem ad se,
And when he had seen him running toward him,
desiliit de curru in occursum ejus,
he leaped down from his chariot to meet him,
Dominus meus misit me ad te dicens:
My lord has sent me to you,
Modo venerunt ad me duo adolescentes de monte Ephraim,
‘Just now two youths from the sons of the prophets have come to me from mount Ephraim.
Give them a talent of silver,
Melius est ut accipias duo talenta.
“It is better that you accept two talents.”
ligavitque duo talenta argenti in duobus saccis,
and he bound the two talents of silver in two bags,
And he set them upon two of his servants,
And when now he had arrived in the evening,
he took them from their hands,
and he stored them in the house.
And Elisha said, “Where are you coming from,
Nonne cor meum in præsenti erat,
quando reversus est homo de curru suo in occursum tui?
when the man turned back from his chariot to meet you?
And now you have received money,
et accepisti vestes ut emas oliveta,
so that you might buy olive groves,
Sed et lepra Naaman adhærebit tibi,
So then, the leprosy of Naaman shall adhere to you,
et semini tuo usque in sempiternum.
Et egressus est ab eo leprosus quasi nix.
And he departed from him a leper, as white as snow.
